newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia firefighters stopped by tollbooth row.
newsitem.headline: Colombia firefighters stopped by tollbooth row.

text.p: Firefighters arrived late to a blaze in central Colombia when over-zealous highway tollbooth attendants refused to let them pass without paying, El Tiempo newspaper reported on Thursday.

Private security staff moved in to douse the flaming row that broke out but instead fanned the flames of discontent when they pulled out their guns and threatened to shoot up the fire trucks if the firefighters did not pay.

The highway holdup took place on Tuesday on the road between Pereira, the state capital of Risaralda province, and neighbouring Valle del Cauca province -- operated as a private concession by multinational security company Wackenhut.
The firefighters finally left without paying but lost vital minutes getting to the inferno at a brick factory less than a mile (one km) away.
Outraged fire chief Maj. Ramon Salcedo told El Tiempo: "In an emergency there's no reason why we should be paying highway tolls, when people know we're carrying out a community service."
Wackenhut officials declined to comment to the newspaper except to say it was "rational" to suppose that in such circumstances emergency vehicles should be allowed through toll gates without paying.
